characters.name: Phil Keoghan (US Host)
characters.description: The long-running host of the originalAmazing Raceseries from the United States, although he's from New Zealand. His main role, aside from exposition, is checking in each team at the end of each leg, with the last team to arrive possibly beingEliminated from the Race. He is normally impartial to the racers, though every so often, he engages inWitty Banterwith certain teams. Popularly regarded as eye candy by the fanbase. Announcer Chatter: Phil starts becoming more talkative in Season 30, when he commentates on teams doing to the Head-to-Head tasks (which were located right next to the Pit Stop). Aside Glance: After Jessica & John's idiotic elimination in Season 22 (where they still held their Express Pass) and John's rather carefreeElimination Statement, a rather shocked Phil turns to the camera, shrugs, and says, "Oy vey!" Author Appeal: Phil is a biking enthusiast, which helps explain why every season has at least one bicycle challenge. Most notable in the Season 20 premiere, where the teams bike to the Starting Line. Berserk Button: Hearing a contestantwanting to quit theRace. He knows better than anyone else that being onThe Amazing Raceand thus getting to travel around the world is a privilege that a relatively small number of people who apply for the show (and there are many) will ever get to do. He looked pissed whenSharikwhined upon reaching the Pit Stop after the Mega Leg that she wanted to go back home to New York, even though she and her father Linton finished in second-to-last place and were not eliminated. Phil told Sharik point blank that if she quits theRace, both she and Linton would be eliminated and be getting on the next flight to New York, basically daring her to leave the show and letting her father down. She didn't do so after that.

characters.name: Allan Wu (Asia and China Host)
characters.description: Host ofThe Amazing Race Asia,China Rush, andChina. The Cameo: Gave out a clue to the racers in US Season 16. Large Ham: He hams up his narrations a lot more often than the other hosts. Mr. Fanservice: Even when compared to the other hosts, Allan tended to wear tight shirts that showed off his arms and physique. One-Steve Limit: Averted withAsia Season 4 contestant Alan Luk.He is the only host so far to avert this trope.

characters.name: Grant Bowler (Australia Host, seasons 1-3)
characters.description: Perma-Stubble: Despite the picture to the right, this is his look most of the time.

characters.name: Beau Ryan (Australia Host, season  4 and onwards)
characters.description: Big Eater: One of the clues in theCelebrity Editionsaid to pick up bachangnotea rice dumpling wrapped in bamboo leaves"because Beau [was] hungry".Beau (after he was asked if he was hungry):I'm always hungry. Butt-Monkey: Invokes this trope at times, due to his comedian experience. Well, admit it -someone needs to test those challenges first... Dramatic Pause: Less fond of this than Grant or Phil, but he still does it from time to time. Fanservice:Showing up at the tannery challenge in season 6 in nothing but a pair of coveralls and a pair of gumboots.Beau being topless in a few episodes in season 6 as he explains challenges and how the Race is going during his isolation period.Goes for a brief swim in Caye Caulker while announcing the Pit Stop. In various shots while checking teams in, he's wearing his swimwear and/or a towel and/or a shirt (although the editing is not seamless and his shirt seems to disappear between two teams arriving).He also goes swimming inthis ad.Appears at the Bollywood dancing Intersection explanation in season 7 without a shirt. Showing up at the tannery challenge in season 6 in nothing but a pair of coveralls and a pair of gumboots.

characters.name: Scott Tweedie (Australia guest host, season 6)
characters.description: Corpsing: Failed to shoot the polo ball while on the bike during the Spoke detour. He manages to do so after getting off the bike, and is reduced to laughter as he finishes. Dramatic Pause: His downplaying of these was carried over from Beau. Game Show Host: As Beau's replacement, he does a lot of hosting similar to Beau himself (such as talking to a Turkish Pit Stop greeter called Hussein - who clearly didn't understand him - in English). Handshake Substitute: Possibly due to COVID precautions, Scotty does fist bumps instead of aGroup Hug. Perma-Stubble: Has about as much as Beau does.

characters.name: Jon Montgomery (Canada Host)
characters.description: Host ofThe Amazing Race Canada. He won the gold medal in the men's skeleton the the Winter Olympics in Vancouver in 2010. Borrowed Catchphrase: He actually used the Roadblock and Detour catchphrases long abandoned by Phil. Growing the Beard: Invoked in interviews for Season 2, as Jon said he was unhappy with his performance in the first season, and claimed he was going to be a much better host in the second. Non-Actor Vehicle: Unlike other hosts, Jon was an athlete, not an actor or other sort of on-camera talent prior to hosting. Product Placement: Chevrolet Corvette and Air Canada sure get mentioned a lot in season 1!

characters.name: Task Judges
characters.description: Ambiguous Gender: In Season 26, one of the task judges in Peru was a clown. After receiving his clue, Tyler said how he could not tell whether the clown was a man or a woman. Beehive Hairdo: Miss Rose, the judge for the trailer setting task in theUnfinished Businessfinale, had a spectacular one that did not budge an inch despite wind constantly destroying the work of all the teams. Chewing the Scenery: Season 21's second Moscow leg had a Roadblock where the team member had to take a test about time zones to be graded by a judge, who took great pleasure in announced repeated failures, as well as relishing the moment when they actually got it correct. Drill Sergeant Nasty: The judge at the Buckingham Palace Detour in Season 25, who chewed out all the teams when they failed to correctly "change the guard." Even when they did the task correctly, he was still mean. Figure It Out Yourself: In many cases, if a racer does not complete a task correctly the judge is not allowed to tell them what they did wrong.
